VI.description: REFERENCE ONLY - todo.txt item 10 (recv.time / parse.time). poc.ip.kria.vi cannot be regenerated by the AIXML tools (FIFO\2C Register and Timed Loop nodes are lost)\2C so this VI shows the timestamp logic of the 156.25 MHz 'PoC IP' Timed Loop with the recommended change already made. Copy the nodes between the comment boxes into poc.ip.kria.vi; do not replace the VI.\0A\0AFACTS established 2026-10-11 from the AIXML export of poc.ip.kria.vi and the netlist sim of the 19\3A37 IP export\3A\0A1. The tick counter (Feedback Node -> Increment -> Select\2C reset on the ip.reset rising edge) lives in the 156.25 MHz loop together with TDATA/TVALID/ip.reset. One tick = one 156.25 MHz cycle = 6.4 ns\2C NOT 10 ns (sim\3A recv.time advances exactly one count per input beat). Every latency figure quoted so far with 10 ns/tick is 1.56x too large.\0A2. bats.parser.vi runs in the OTHER Timed Loop (100 MHz\2C with the CMD/DEBUG outputs). Its `time` input comes from a Register read; the Register (written with the counter every cycle in the 156 MHz loop) IS the clock-domain crossing. A wire from the counter to the parser is impossible between two Timed Loops\2C so the register read STAYS. Its lag (1-3 ticks\2C 6-19 ns) is the price of the crossing; parse.time is therefore a few ticks late\2C never early.\0A3. Today recv.time is wired straight from the counter into the stream cluster that enters the CDC FIFO\2C so each CMD record carries the arrival tick of the word that completed its message (per-word stamp). The frame-start latch that existed before 2026-10-11 is gone.\0A\0ARECOMMENDED CHANGE (the only diagram change)\3A put the frame-start latch back\2C i.e. recv.time \3A= counter when `data valid` rises (first word of a frame)\2C else hold the previous value. Then parse.time - recv.time is 'time since the first byte of the packet arrived'\2C the quantity a trading system cares about\2C the figure is comparable with the earlier measurements\2C and the host tools can group a frame's records by equal recv.time. The latch is the Not / Feedback Node / And / Select / Feedback Node group in the box 'CHANGE - frame-start latch'.\0A\0AALTERNATIVE (no diagram change)\3A keep the per-word stamp. Then parse.time - recv.time is the parser's own per-message latency (1 tick for a message completed by the arriving word\2C more for messages queued behind it) and Claude switches eval_sim.py / decode_capture.py to group by sequence number. Tell Claude which one you chose.\0A\0AHOST SIDE (Claude does this)\3A TICK_NS 10 -> 6.4 in apps/poc_inject/decode_capture.py and ip_export/netlist_sim/eval_sim.py; CLAUDE.md latency figures re-stated in 6.4 ns ticks.\0A\0ARun this VI\3A ip.reset = [T\2CF\2CF\2C...]\2C data valid = [F\2CF\2CT\2CT\2CT\2CF\2CF\2CT\2CT\2CF]. Expect tick = 0\2C1\2C2\2C...; first word of frame = T at indexes 2 and 7; recv.time = 0\2C0\2C2\2C2\2C2\2C2\2C2\2C7\2C7\2C7.

FreeLabel.comment: REFERENCE SNIPPET for todo item 10 - read the VI description (Ctrl-I).\0AOne loop iteration = one cycle of the 156.25 MHz PoC IP Timed Loop in poc.ip.kria.vi.\0AInputs/outputs are arrays only so the VI can be run on My Computer; in poc.ip.kria.vi they are the plain wires named in the boxes.

UNCHANGED - tick counter as it is in poc.ip.kria.vi (156.25 MHz loop)\3A\0AFeedback Node -> Increment -> Select (t = 0\2C s = ip.reset rising edge\2C f = x+1).\0AOne tick = 6.4 ns. Keep the Register WRITE of this wire\3A it is the clock-domain crossing\0Athat bats.parser.vi (100 MHz loop) reads as `time`. That Register read cannot be replaced by a wire.

CHANGE - frame-start latch (insert between the counter wire and the Bundle By Name\0Athat writes recv.time into My.Network.Data.Stream\2C right before the CDC FIFO write)\3A\0Afirst word = data valid AND NOT Feedback(data valid)\0Arecv.time = first word ? counter \3A Feedback(recv.time)\0AToday recv.time is wired straight from the counter (per-word stamp).

-> recv.time element of the My.Network.Data.Stream Bundle By Name (CDC FIFO write).\0AAfter the change every record of a frame carries the arrival tick of the frame's first word.\0AALTERNATIVE\3A leave poc.ip.kria.vi as it is (per-word stamp) and tell Claude to switch the host grouping.
